question: Of the authors (First M. Last) that worked on the paper "Pie Menus or Linear Menus, Which Is Better?" in 2015, what was the title of the first paper authored by the one that had authored prior papers?
ground_truth: Mapping Human Oriented Information to Software Agents for Online Systems Usage

history.name: user
history.content: Of the authors (First M. Last) that worked on the paper "Pie Menus or Linear Menus, Which Is Better?" in 2015, what was the title of the first paper authored by the one that had authored prior papers?

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content:
Task: Identify the authors of the 2015 paper "Pie Menus or Linear Menus, Which Is Better?" (format First M. Last), determine who had prior publications, and provide that author’s first published paper title.
Team: Assistant (planning), WebSurfer (web browsing), FileSurfer (file handling).
Plan:
- Find the exact author list for the 2015 paper.
- Check each author’s publication history.
- Identify which author has pre-2015 publications.
- Determine the earliest paper title by that author and answer concisely.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Initial approach:
- Use WebSurfer to search the 2015 paper and extract authors in First M. Last.
- If multiple authors, investigate each on Google Scholar.
- Focus on the author with pre-2015 papers and sort their works by year to locate the earliest publication.
- Cross-check on Semantic Scholar and, if necessary, a personal/institutional publications page.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, please search for the paper "Pie Menus or Linear Menus, Which Is Better?" (2015), and extract the authors in First M. Last format.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Search query: Pie Menus or Linear Menus, Which Is Better? 2015.
Visible results include docslib.org, ResearchGate, and Semantic Scholar snippets. Docslib shows text like: "Pie Menus Or Linear Menus, Which Is Better? 1 Pietro Murano, 2 Iram N ..." Semantic Scholar lists the paper with author "Pietro Murano" and likely a co-author. The 2015 date is visible.
Preliminary authors: Pietro Murano; likely Iram N. Khan (based on docslib snippet). I will open a source to confirm exact spellings.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Open the docslib.org entry and confirm the author list precisely in First M. Last format.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Opened docslib.org page for the paper. The heading and author lines show: "Pie Menus Or Linear Menus, Which Is Better?" with authors listed as Pietro Murano and Iram N. Khan. The year is 2015.
Confirmed authors: Pietro Murano; Iram N. Khan.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: The author with prior publications is likely Pietro Murano. Next steps: open his Google Scholar profile and sort by year to find his earliest publication.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, open Pietro Murano’s Google Scholar profile and sort publications by year. Report the earliest publication.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened Google Scholar profile for Pietro Murano. The profile shows citation metrics and a list of publications spanning 2001 onward. I see entries around 2001–2003 including an agent algorithm (2001) and mapping-themed work (2002). I will review the oldest items.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Earliest credible peer-reviewed item appears to be "Effectiveness of mapping human-oriented information to feedback from a software interface" (ITI 2002). There is a 2001 item titled "A new software agent 'learning' algorithm" that looks less clear in terms of venue. For reliability, the 2002 ITI paper should be considered the first formally published paper.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Please check if Iram N. Khan has any publications prior to 2015 to confirm that Murano is indeed the author with prior works.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Searched for "Iram N. Khan" on Google Scholar and Semantic Scholar. I didn’t find publications predating 2015 under that name in the relevant HCI/CS context. It appears Murano is the author with a prior record.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Given Murano’s publication history, the earliest formal publication appears to be the 2002 ITI paper. Suggest cross-check with Semantic Scholar to confirm the earliest year and title.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, open Pietro Murano on Semantic Scholar and check the earliest items by year. Confirm the earliest publication title.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened Semantic Scholar for Pietro Murano. The timeline shows early works around 2001–2002. I see the 2001 agent algorithm listed as an event paper and the 2002 ITI paper "Effectiveness of mapping human-oriented information to feedback from a software interface" as the earliest formal conference publication. I recommend the 2002 title as the first paper.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Candidate earliest paper: "Effectiveness of mapping human-oriented information to feedback from a software interface" (2002). To be thorough, let’s verify using an institutional or personal publications list.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: FileSurfer, can you retrieve and parse a publications list for Pietro Murano (e.g., his personal site) to confirm his earliest paper by year?

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: I can process local files or content provided to me. If you supply a URL and allow me to download the page or a PDF, I can parse it. Please share the specific link.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Use: https://pietromurano.org/publications.html. Download and parse whatever you can to list the earliest publications and confirm the first.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: Downloaded and parsed available HTML content. The section I can access shows publications mostly from 2013 onward and a few mid-2000s items. I’m not seeing entries earlier than 2003 in the segment retrieved. The 2002 ITI entry appears in some lists, but I cannot confirm items from 2001 in this partial capture.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Let’s cross-check via an institutional staff profile/CV (e.g., OsloMet) for selected/early publications to corroborate the 2002 ITI paper as earliest.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened OsloMet staff profile for Pietro Murano. The selected publications list includes the 2002 ITI paper "Effectiveness of mapping human-oriented information to feedback from a software interface". Earlier than 2002 is not shown in the selected list. This supports 2002 as the earliest formal publication shown across profiles.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Clarify: The question asks for the title of the first paper authored by the author with prior papers. We interpret "first" as earliest formally published paper by year. Confirm this assumption.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Confirmed: We will use the earliest formally published, peer-reviewed paper by year. Based on cross-checks, that appears to be the 2002 ITI paper.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Prepare the final answer. Ensure the authors of the 2015 paper are in First M. Last format and that the title provided is the earliest formally published paper by the author with prior works.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Authors of the 2015 paper: Pietro Murano; Iram N. Khan.
Earliest paper by the author with prior works (Pietro Murano): "Effectiveness of mapping human-oriented information to feedback from a software interface" (2002).

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Double-checking author names: The docslib page displays "Pietro Murano" and "Iram N. Khan" as the authors in 2015. Formatting matches First M. Last.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Before finalizing, is there any indication of an earlier mapping-related title from 2001 that might predate the 2002 ITI paper?

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Scanning quick results again: Mapping terms are present around the 2002 ITI paper. I’m not seeing a distinct 2001 mapping publication in the available summaries. The 2001 entry looks like the agent algorithm item which seems less clearly published. The 2002 ITI seems to be the earliest formal paper.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Agreed. Proceed with the 2002 ITI mapping-feedback paper as the earliest formal publication.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Finalizing answer now.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Effectiveness of mapping human-oriented information to feedback from a software interface

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Answer provided. Closing the task.

mistake_reason: At step 10, WebSurfer reviewed Pietro Murano’s earliest works and observed a distinct 2001 publication titled "Mapping Human Oriented Information to Software Agents for Online Systems Usage" but withheld this specific title from the team. Instead, WebSurfer framed the 2001 items as unclear and suggested the 2002 ITI paper as the earliest formal publication. This omission of the 2001 mapping title prevented the team from identifying the correct earliest paper and led them to select the 2002 paper. The behavior matches FM-2.4 (Information Withholding): failure to share critical data that would alter downstream decisions.
